attempts.paper_title: A VTA-pontine GABA pathway biases locomotor direction via local and distal inhibition
attempts.entry_title: VTA-PnO pathway and dopamine photometry (Gonzalez-Cabrera et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Only the paper's photometry finding could be tested here, and it held up: continuous light on VTA-PnO neurons raised the calcium signal of dopamine neurons, 5 to 20 Hz trains did not, and the rise was larger than in control mice. Both results depend on how the paper computed its post hoc tests, which it does not say; with a separate t-test per frequency neither holds. The tracing, juxtacellular, slice and backward walking findings could not be tested because their data are not in the dataset. The opto-tagged unit recordings could not be analysed either: the files hold raw voltage without sorted units, and the paper's hand-curated spike sort cannot be repeated.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gonzalez-Cabrera et al. (2026) on dandiset 001955, which holds fiber photometry of VTA dopamine neurons during optogenetic stimulation of VTA-PnO neurons in 5 opsin and 3 control mice, and raw acute and chronic silicon-probe recordings. The two photometry findings of Figure 3b,c are tested. The silicon-probe findings cannot be tested, as the files hold no sorted units and the paper's sort and curation cannot be repeated, and the juxtacellular, slice, tracing and open-field experiments are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: In opsin mice, VTA-PnO stimulation raises the DA population calcium signal above its pre-stimulus level with continuous light, but not with 5, 10 or 20 Hz trains.
outcomes.source: Figure 3b legend; Results, Optogenetic activation of VTA PnO elevates dopaminergic population signals, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Within-opsin pre-post comparison was significant at continuous stimulation, with 5-20 Hz yielding non-significant differences
outcomes.notes: Over 5 opsin mice, 4 conditions, 23 trials per file (13 in the photometry-exp-5 files, 15 at 5 Hz, where all intervals are used). With the ordinary two-way ANOVA epoch by frequency and the post hoc comparisons on its residual mean square, as Prism computes them, continuous light raises the z-scored signal with BH-corrected p from 3.8e-06 to 3.8e-05 in all 32 readings, below the criterion's 0.0001 in each, and 5, 10 and 20 Hz are not significant in any (20 Hz p at least 0.44). Under the main reading (Methods baseline, mean and SD z, epoch means, 100 Hz) Stim minus Pre is 7.10 z for continuous light (SE 1.209, df 32, BH p 6.3e-06; 1.92 to 15.00 per mouse, positive in 5 of 5) and 0.18, 0.55 and 1.40 z at 5, 10 and 20 Hz. Under the Methods baseline with mean and SD z the Pre values are fixed at 0; there the ordinary form's SE equals the paired pooled-difference form's (both 1.209), and its smaller p comes only from df 32 against 16, the extra df from the Pre cells. The readings with the code's -3.0 s baseline, where Pre varies, give p 9.9e-06 to 3.8e-05 under the ordinary form. Among the paired forms, the pooled-difference form (Stim - Pre variance averaged over the four frequencies, df 16, not one of Prism's forms) holds in 20 of 32 readings, the main reading among them (BH p 9.4e-05), so a paired reading also gives reproduced. With the repeated-measures ANOVA and Prism's error with sphericity assumed (epoch x frequency x subject mean square, df 12), continuous light gives BH p 2.0e-04 to 5.3e-04 in all 32 readings with the trains not significant, which the criterion counts as partially reproduced. With a separate paired t-test per frequency (Prism without sphericity), continuous light gives BH p 0.072 to 0.11 (uncorrected 0.04 under the main reading), so the claim would not be reproduced. No train frequency reaches p < 0.05 in any form or reading (smallest 0.072). The 470-nm signal without the 405-nm fit gives the same pattern (ordinary form p 7.5e-06 to 4.1e-05 in 16 of 16 readings). The epoch by frequency interaction p is 0.0006 to 0.0078 over readings. The claims file's criterion asks for a paired post hoc comparison, which the ordinary ANOVA's comparison is not; this is asked of a reader (questions/gonzalez-cabrera-2026.yaml). Which ANOVA and post hoc error the paper used is for the authors (findings, methods_unavailable). The stimulation table shares the signal's clock in the opsin continuous files (mean change 0.0410 dF/F at the onsets against -0.0010 and -0.0015 with onsets shifted by 6.5 s, and larger than both shifts in each of the 5 opsin mice).
deviations: Assumption. The legend says "two-way ANOVA with FDR-corrected post hoc comparisons" and the Methods (Quantification and statistical analysis) name GraphPad Prism v10; neither says whether the ANOVA had repeated measures or how the comparisons were computed. The ordinary two-way ANOVA (a reading the claims file names) is assumed, since this legend does not name repeated measures where the Figure 2f and 2i legends do ("one-way ANOVA with repeated measures"); this support is weak, and nothing else in the paper decides between the designs. Its post hoc comparisons use the model's residual mean square, as Prism computes them after an ordinary two-way ANOVA (GraphPad, "How Prism 8.0 computes multiple comparisons tests following ANOVA" (cdn.graphpad.com/faq/1688/file/MulitpleComparisonAlgorithmsPrism8.pdf)). This comparison is not paired, as the criterion's "post hoc paired" asks; a reader is asked. The repeated-measures forms (Prism with and without sphericity) and a pooled-difference form are run and shown.

The photometry preprocessing follows the paper's code (Fiber_Photometry_PSTH.ipynb at commit 1ff5196), as the claims file's criterion says; the Methods' "downsampled" gives no rate, and 100 Hz block means are a standard choice, with the native 12-kHz rate run as a variant (same outcomes).
The code's guard that drops trials with under 1 s of baseline would drop every trial under the Methods' 0.9-s baseline, so it is applied only with the code's -3.0 s baseline, where it drops none.

All stimulation intervals are used, as the code uses every event; photometry-exp-5 at 5 Hz has two extra 3.0-s intervals before its regular train, and the result without them (the intervals within 20 ms of the file's median length, which keeps every interval of the other 31 files) is shown (same outcomes).

The clock shared by the stimulation table and the signal is shown only for the opsin continuous files; for the train and control files, where the response is too small to show it, it is assumed from the same table format and 13-s cycle.

outcomes.statement: The stimulation-evoked change in DA calcium signal (Stim minus Pre) is larger in opsin mice than in controls for continuous light only, not for 5-20 Hz.
outcomes.source: Figure 3c legend; Results, Optogenetic activation of VTA PnO elevates dopaminergic population signals, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: change-scores (Δ = Stim-Pre) were larger in the opsin group compared to the controls (n = 3) for continuous illumination only, with no effects at 5-20 Hz
outcomes.notes: 5 opsin and 3 control mice. With Prism's error, the within-cell mean square of the group by frequency cells (df 24), which Prism uses after the ordinary two-way ANOVA and, with sphericity assumed, after the mixed design, the opsin change is larger than the control change for continuous light in all 64 rows of that form (32 readings, each with either ANOVA; BH p 0.00074 to 0.0028, the legend reports 0.002), and 5, 10 and 20 Hz are not significant in any (20 Hz p at least 0.66). Under the main reading the continuous change is 7.10 z in opsin mice and 0.12 in controls, a difference of 6.98 z (SE 1.614, df 24, BH p 0.00092), and at 5, 10 and 20 Hz the opsin minus control differences are 0.14, 0.27 and 1.52 z. With a separate unpaired t-test per frequency (Prism without sphericity) the continuous difference is not significant in any reading (BH p 0.13 to 0.19), so under that form the claim is not reproduced. The 470-nm signal without the 405-nm fit gives the same result with Prism's error in 16 of 16 readings (BH p 0.00071 to 0.0022). The group by frequency interaction p is 0.016 to 0.038 over readings.
deviations: Assumption. The legend gives "two-way ANOVA with FDR-corrected post hoc comparisons" and the Methods name GraphPad Prism v10, without saying how the comparisons were computed. Prism's error is assumed (GraphPad, "How Prism 8.0 computes multiple comparisons tests following ANOVA" (cdn.graphpad.com/faq/1688/file/MulitpleComparisonAlgorithmsPrism8.pdf)): after an ordinary two-way ANOVA every comparison uses MS(Residual); after the mixed design with sphericity assumed, a comparison of the unmatched groups at one level of the repeated factor uses (SS(Subjects) + SS(Residuals)) / (DF(Subjects) + DF(Residuals)); both equal the within-cell mean square with df 24, so both designs give the same p. Under the ordinary ANOVA adopted for fig3b-photometry-continuous-only this needs no assumption about sphericity. Separate unpaired t-tests (Prism without sphericity) are run and shown.

The photometry preprocessing follows the paper's code (Fiber_Photometry_PSTH.ipynb at commit 1ff5196), as the claims file's criterion says; the Methods' "downsampled" gives no rate, and 100 Hz block means are a standard choice, with the native 12-kHz rate run as a variant (same outcomes).
The code's guard that drops trials with under 1 s of baseline would drop every trial under the Methods' 0.9-s baseline, so it is applied only with the code's -3.0 s baseline, where it drops none.

All stimulation intervals are used, as the code uses every event; photometry-exp-5 at 5 Hz has two extra 3.0-s intervals before its regular train, and the result without them (the intervals within 20 ms of the file's median length, which keeps every interval of the other 31 files) is shown (same outcomes).

The clock shared by the stimulation table and the signal is shown only for the opsin continuous files; for the train and control files, where the response is too small to show it, it is assumed from the same table format and 13-s cycle.

findings.statement: The 34 ecephys files (25 acute, 9 chronic, 161 GB) hold only raw broadband voltage and unnamed ADC series. They have no units table or spike times, no opto-tagging result, no intervals or event tables, and no processing module, so none of the paper's 15 silicon-probe findings (Figure 3d-k, Figure 4, Supplementary Figures 3b-d and 4) can be tested without redoing the spike sorting and its manual curation in Phy 2. The dandiset description's "synchronized information describing rotation onset, direction, timing, and experimental condition" is not in the files as labelled data: the rotation onsets are only on an unnamed ADC channel, and the direction is nowhere.

The ADC series are named only by number (ADC1 to ADC8). A scan of every channel of every recording finds 133 tagging trains of 210 1-ms pulses at 5 Hz, on ADC1 (69), ADC2 (45) or ADC3 (19), with the same amplitude, but nothing says which is the 470-nm and which the 635-nm laser. Trains of 2-s pulses on ADC1 of 16 chronic recordings match the rotarod bouts, but nothing says which block is reverse and which forward. Trains of 1-s pulses (the 1-s light protocol) are on ADC1 or ADC2, and some recordings carry trains of 3-s or 4-s pulses that the Methods do not describe. Which recording is the baseline, tagging, 1-s light or rotarod block is not recorded.
The electrode location is "unknown" for every channel of every ecephys file.

The chronic files come from 4 subjects (DAT-2598-H8 with 6 sessions, DAT-2677-H10, DAT-2680 and DAT-2749 with one each); the paper reports chronic recordings from 3 mice. Which subjects and sessions the paper's 40 units and 17 bidirectional units come from is not stated.

The juxtacellular, tracing, ex vivo slice and open-field experiments (24 of the paper's 41 findings) are not in the dandiset. The Zenodo record it cites (doi 10.5281/zenodo.21390830) holds figure-level source tables, histology images of Figure 1a and eight open-field videos without DeepLabCut tracking.

In the photometry files, session_start_time is often earlier than the end of the previous file of the same mouse (for example photometry-control-1 at 20 Hz starts at 11:02:36 and lasts 462 s, and its continuous file starts at 11:04:16), so it is not the time recording started; it looks like a file export time.

photometry-exp-5 at 5 Hz has two 3.0-s stimulation intervals, 8 s apart, at 3.8 s and 11.8 s, before its regular train of 2.8-s intervals every 13 s; they are not described. All other files have only intervals of their condition's length. photometry-exp-5 has 13 trials per condition, the others 23.

In many photometry files the isosbestic fit explains little of the GCaMP signal (R squared under 0.30, the level at which the paper's own code warns, in 12 of 32 files, from -0.01 to 0.99 over files, computed over whole recordings), which the code reports but does not act on.

paper_notes.statement: For Figure 3b,c the paper gives "two-way ANOVA with FDR-corrected post hoc comparisons" in GraphPad Prism v10, without saying whether the ANOVA had repeated measures, whether sphericity was assumed, or how the post hoc comparisons were computed. The outcome depends on it: for Figure 3b, continuous light gives BH p 3.8e-06 to 3.8e-05 with the ordinary two-way ANOVA and its residual error, 2.0e-04 to 5.3e-04 with the repeated-measures error, and 0.072 to 0.11 with separate paired t-tests; for Figure 3c, 0.00074 to 0.0028 with the pooled error and 0.13 to 0.19 with separate unpaired t-tests. Which design and post hoc error were used?

The silicon-probe units were sorted with Kilosort and curated by hand in Phy 2, with no Kilosort version, parameters or curation criteria given, and the sorted units are not deposited. Which version and parameters were used, by what criteria were clusters accepted, and could the curated units (spike times and cluster labels) be added to the dandiset?

entries.name: gonzalez-cabrera-2026
entries.title: VTA-PnO pathway and dopamine photometry (Gonzalez-Cabrera et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gonzalez-Cabrera et al. (2026) on dandiset 001955, which holds fiber photometry of VTA dopamine neurons during optogenetic stimulation of VTA-PnO neurons in 5 opsin and 3 control mice, and raw acute and chronic silicon-probe recordings. The two photometry findings of Figure 3b,c are tested. The silicon-probe findings cannot be tested, as the files hold no sorted units and the paper's sort and curation cannot be repeated, and the juxtacellular, slice, tracing and open-field experiments are not in the dandiset.
